context.body: Judgment and compassion alternate inside a worsening cycle.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The LORD’s anger gives Israel into enemies, mercy raises judges, and judgment tests the nations when Israel repeatedly turns away.
observations.label: God responds to Israel’s recurring abandonment: action

observations.body: Israel serves, forgets, cries under oppression, follows judges briefly, and becomes more corrupt after they die.
observations.label: God responds to Israel’s recurring abandonment: response

observations.body: forsook · anger · raised up judges · had compassion · tested
observations.label: Words in Judges 2:6–23

payload.posture: Read Judges 2:6–23 as land, judges, and kings evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The nations are retained both as consequence and test, leaving Israel’s responsibility intact.
payload.title: God responds to Israel’s recurring abandonment
